subject: physics
title: Domestic uses and safety
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Domestic uses and safety — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.2.3.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Domestic uses and safety, specification section 4.2.3.
final_note: You worked through Domestic uses and safety — 12 specification statements.

concepts.def: A potential difference that repeatedly changes direction, so the current it drives repeatedly reverses direction round the circuit. Mains electricity is an ac supply.
A potential difference that is always in the same direction, so the current it drives passes round the circuit in one direction only. Cells and batteries supply a direct potential difference.
The ac supply delivered to homes in the United Kingdom: a frequency of 50 Hz and a potential difference of about 230 V.
The number of complete cycles of an alternating supply each second, measured in hertz (Hz). A 50 Hz supply completes 50 cycles every second.
The cable used to connect most electrical appliances to the mains. It contains three wires: live, neutral and earth.
The brown wire, which carries the alternating potential difference from the supply. It is at about 230 V relative to earth.
The blue wire, which completes the circuit. It is at, or close to, earth potential (0 V).
The green and yellow striped wire. It is a safety wire, at 0 V, which stops the appliance becoming live; it only carries a current if there is a fault.
The potential of the ground, taken as 0 V. The potential difference between the live wire and earth is about 230 V, which is why any connection from live to earth is dangerous.
The insulation covering each wire is colour coded for easy identification: live wire brown, neutral wire blue, earth wire green and yellow stripes.
What happens when a fault lets the live wire touch the metal case of an appliance, raising the case to about 230 V. The earth wire is there to stop this.
Any path joining the live wire to earth, including a person touching the live wire while in contact with the ground. A large current passes along it because there is about 230 V across it.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes the electricity supply in a UK home?
options: An alternating supply, of about 230 V, with a frequency of 50 Hz
A direct supply, of about 230 V, with a frequency of 50 Hz
An alternating supply, of 50 V, at a frequency of 230 Hz
A direct supply, of a steady 230 V, with no frequency
mcqs.explain: Mains electricity is an ac supply; in the United Kingdom it has a frequency of 50 Hz and is about 230 V.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a direct and an alternating potential difference?
options: A direct pd stays the same size, but an alternating pd changes size
A direct pd is always low, but an alternating pd is always big
A direct pd acts one way only; an alternating pd keeps reversing
A direct pd comes from the mains; an alternating pd from a cell
mcqs.explain: A direct potential difference is always in the same direction; an alternating one repeatedly changes direction.

mcqs.q: A student connects an oscilloscope first to a cell and then to a low-voltage supply at mains frequency. Which description of the two traces is correct?
options: Both traces are flat lines, but the mains line sits much higher up
The cell gives a flat line; the mains trace crosses zero
The cell trace crosses the zero line; the mains gives a flat line
Both traces cross zero, but the mains trace is taller
mcqs.explain: A cell gives a direct pd, drawn as a flat line; the mains pd reverses, so its trace goes above and below zero.

mcqs.q: The UK mains supply has a frequency of 50 Hz. What does this tell you?
options: The pd completes 50 full cycles every minute
The supply transfers 50 J of energy each second
The pd between live and neutral is about 50 V
The pd goes through 50 cycles each second
mcqs.explain: Hertz means cycles per second, so a 50 Hz supply completes 50 complete cycles each second.

mcqs.q: Most electrical appliances are connected to the mains using three-core cable. What are the three cores?
options: Two live wires together with one neutral wire
The live wire, the neutral wire and the earth wire
The live wire, the neutral wire and a fuse wire
The live wire, the earth wire and a switch
mcqs.explain: Three-core cable contains a live wire, a neutral wire and an earth wire.

mcqs.q: The insulation on the wires in a three-core cable is colour coded. Which row gives the colours correctly?
options: Live brown, neutral blue, earth is plain green
Live red, neutral black, earth green and yellow
Live blue, neutral brown, earth green and yellow stripes
Live brown, neutral blue, earth green and yellow
mcqs.explain: The specified colour code: live wire brown, neutral wire blue, earth wire green and yellow stripes.

mcqs.q: A wire inside a plug is covered in blue insulation. What is the job of this wire?
options: It completes the circuit back to the supply
It carries the alternating pd from the supply
It carries current away only if there is a fault
It holds the case of the appliance at 0 V
mcqs.explain: Blue is the neutral wire, and the neutral wire completes the circuit.

mcqs.q: Why is the insulation covering each wire in a cable colour coded?
options: So that each wire can carry a different sized current
Because coloured plastics insulate at a higher voltage
So that each wire can be identified easily
So the colour shows which wire is at the highest pd
mcqs.explain: The insulation covering each wire is colour coded for easy identification.

mcqs.q: What is the job of the live wire in a mains circuit?
options: It takes the current back to the supply after the appliance
It carries a current only if a fault develops in the case
It stops the metal case of the appliance becoming live
It carries the alternating potential difference from the supply
mcqs.explain: The live wire carries the alternating potential difference from the supply.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of the earth wire in an appliance with a metal case?
options: It is a safety wire that stops the appliance becoming live
It completes the circuit so that a current can pass round
It carries the used current away to the ground all the time
It supplies the alternating pd to the metal case
mcqs.explain: The earth wire is a safety wire, there to stop the appliance becoming live.

mcqs.q: A kettle is plugged in and working. Which row gives the potential differences correctly?
options: Live to earth about 230 V; neutral to earth about 230 V
Live to earth about 115 V; neutral to earth also 115 V
Live to earth about 230 V; neutral to earth about 0 V
Live to earth about 0 V; neutral to earth is 230 V
mcqs.explain: The pd between the live wire and earth (0 V) is about 230 V; the neutral wire is at, or close to, 0 V.

mcqs.q: When does a current pass along the earth wire of an appliance?
options: Whenever the appliance is on
Only when there is a fault
All the time it is plugged in
Whenever the current gets large
mcqs.explain: The earth wire is at 0 V and only carries a current if there is a fault.

mcqs.q: A lamp is switched off at a switch in the mains circuit, but is still plugged in. Why can the live wire still be dangerous?
options: Opening the switch only lowers the pd to a smaller, safer value
The neutral wire feeds a current back along the live wire
It is still at about 230 V relative to earth up to the open switch
The earth wire raises the lamp's case to about 230 V
mcqs.explain: The supply is still connected, so the live wire on the supply side of the open switch stays at about 230 V.

mcqs.q: A person changes a bulb without unplugging the lamp. The switch is open. Standing on a concrete floor, they touch the live contact and receive a shock. Why?
options: The earth wire pushes a current out of the ground up through them
The contact is still at 230 V, so a current passes through them
Their body completes the circuit between live and neutral
The open switch sends the current out along another wire
mcqs.explain: An open switch does not remove the pd, so touching the live contact while on the floor makes a live-to-earth path.

mcqs.q: A frayed cable lets the bare live wire touch a metal water pipe that runs into the ground. Why is this dangerous?
options: No current can pass at all, so the wire overheats and melts
The pd across the appliance rises well above 230 V
The current in the neutral wire immediately changes direction
There is 230 V across the path, so a large current passes
mcqs.explain: Live is about 230 V above earth, and the path has little resistance, so a very large current passes.

mcqs.q: Why is touching the live wire while standing on wet ground so dangerous, even though only one wire is touched?
options: A current passes through them to earth
The wet ground stops the earth wire working
The pd across the appliance is now doubled
The water raises the pd across them to 460 V
mcqs.explain: The body provides a connection between the live wire and earth, so a current passes through it.
